proposals.before: Promoted to judicial investigator at Yanping and then appointed investigating censor on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, he impeached Dashi Timur, left chancellor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, for betraying the state. Invoking the Han precedent of Emperor Gaozu executing Lord Ding, he argued to make plain the supreme duty owed by a subject to his sovereign.
proposals.after: Transferred to assistant prefect of Yanping and then appointed investigating censor on the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, he impeached Dashi Timur, left chancellor of the Liaoyang Branch Secretariat, for betraying the state. Invoking the Han precedent of Emperor Gaozu executing Lord Ding, he argued to make plain the supreme duty owed by a subject to his sovereign.
proposals.reason: Chinese 轉延平判官 is a transfer to panguan, already rendered assistant prefect at Jiangyin, not judicial investigator; 行臺 is a branch censorate.

proposals.before: Recalled to serve again as investigating censor, Liangzhen judged that with the emperor now personally attending to the myriad affairs of government, he could not afford to neglect recruiting worthy advisers. He therefore submitted a series of memorials: "During the Tianshun era the laws and institutions fell into grave disorder and the vital energies of the dynasty were grievously depleted.
proposals.after: Recalled to serve again as investigating censor, Liangzhen judged that with the emperor now personally attending to the myriad affairs of government, he could not afford to neglect recruiting worthy advisers. He therefore submitted a series of memorials: "During the Tianli years the laws and institutions fell into grave disorder and the vital energies of the dynasty were grievously depleted.
proposals.reason: 天曆 is the Yuan Tianli era, not the Ming Tianshun era.

proposals.before: He also said that by national custom, when the father dies one marries his father's younger brother's wife; when a brother dies one takes his brother's wife; when parents die there is no mourning observance—thereupon he said: "The constants of human relations all come from Heaven and cannot be changed; yet the officials who deliberate on law say that Mongols are not bound by this rule and that people of the various states each follow their native customs.
proposals.after: He also said that by national custom, when the father dies one marries his stepmother; when a brother dies one takes his brother's wife; when parents die there is no mourning observance—thereupon he said: "The constants of human relations all come from Heaven and cannot be changed; yet the officials who deliberate on law say that Mongols are not bound by this rule and that people of the various states each follow their native customs.
proposals.reason: 從母 is stepmother/mother's sister, not father's younger brother's wife.

proposals.before: When a eunuch named Han, having lost a favored concubine, killed his wife, minced her flesh, and fed it to his dogs, Liangzhen memorialized asking that the severest penalty be imposed. He also argued that eunuchs who colluded with court officials to obstruct government were a grave evil and ought to be purged.
proposals.after: When the eunuch Hanshi's favored concubine killed his wife, minced her flesh, and fed it to dogs, Liangzhen memorialized asking that the severest penalty be imposed. He also argued that eunuchs who colluded with court officials to obstruct government were a grave evil and ought to be purged.
proposals.reason: 宦者罕失 is a transliterated personal name; 嬖妾殺其妻 makes the concubine the killer rather than 失 as the verb lost.

proposals.before: Earlier the Taizhou rebel Zhang Shicheng had surrendered and then rebelled again, killing Zhao Lian, participant in government of the Huainan Branch Secretariat, and seizing Gaoyou and Luhe. Grand Preceptor Toghto received orders to command the armies of the imperial princes on a southern campaign, and Liangzhen went with him, accompanied by Participant Gong Bojuan, Lu Shan of the Ministry of Punishments, and others.
proposals.after: Earlier the Taizhou rebel Zhang Shicheng had surrendered and then rebelled again, killing Zhao Lian, participant in government of the Huainan Branch Secretariat, and seizing Gaoyou and Luhe. Grand Preceptor Toghto received orders to command the armies of the imperial princes on a southern campaign, and Liangzhen went with him, accompanied by Participant Gong Bosui, Lu Shan of the Ministry of Punishments, and others.
proposals.reason: 龔伯璲 uses 璲 (suì); English Bojuan misreads the given name and should be Bosui.

proposals.before: Earlier, the Taizhou bandit Zhang Shicheng had submitted and then rebelled again, killing Participant in Government Zhao Lian of the Huainan Branch Secretariat and advancing to occupy Gaoyou and Luhe; Grand Preceptor Toghto received the edict and commanded the armies of the imperial princes on a southern campaign, and Liangzhen together with Participant Gong Bojuan, director of affairs Lu Shan of the Ministry of Punishments, and others followed him.
proposals.after: Earlier, the Taizhou bandit Zhang Shicheng had submitted and then rebelled again, killing Participant in Government Zhao Lian of the Huainan Branch Secretariat and advancing to occupy Gaoyou and Luhe; Grand Preceptor Toghto received the edict and commanded the armies of the imperial princes on a southern campaign, and Liangzhen together with Participant Gong Bosui, director of affairs Lu Shan of the Ministry of Punishments, and others followed him.
proposals.reason: Same given-name error: 伯璲 is Bosui, not Bojuan.

proposals.before: He once argued that the Zhizheng code's gradations of punishment were inconsistent, allowing clerks to exploit the gaps for fraud. He nominated several experts in the Ming code to consult past and present precedents and redraft the statutes. The new code was completed, but the project was abandoned.
proposals.after: He once argued that the Zhizheng code's gradations of punishment were inconsistent, allowing clerks to exploit the gaps for fraud. He nominated several experts well versed in the statutes to consult past and present precedents and redraft the law book. The new code was completed, but the project was abandoned.
proposals.reason: 明律者 means men who understood the penal statutes clearly, not experts in a Ming-dynasty code.

proposals.before: He once argued that the Zhizheng code's gradations of severity were inconsistent, allowing clerks to exploit both and commit fraud; he nominated several who understood the Ming code, consulted past and present, and redrafted the law book—the book was completed but the project was abandoned.
proposals.after: He once argued that the Zhizheng code's gradations of severity were inconsistent, allowing clerks to exploit both and commit fraud; he nominated several who understood the statutes clearly, consulted past and present, and redrafted the law book—the book was completed but the project was abandoned.
proposals.reason: 明律 is 'understand the statutes clearly,' not 'the Ming code.'

proposals.before: In 1352 Grand Tutor and Right Chancellor Toghto returned to power. When the river breach was discussed, wishing to relieve the people's suffering and fulfill the imperial mandate, he convened the court for collective deliberation—but every minister had a different opinion.
proposals.after: In 1349 Grand Tutor and Right Chancellor Toghto returned to power. When the river breach was discussed, wishing to relieve the people's suffering and fulfill the imperial mandate, he convened the court for collective deliberation—but every minister had a different opinion.
proposals.reason: 九年 in the Zhizheng sequence of this biography is AD 1349; 1352 contradicts the following eleventh-year date of 1351.

proposals.before: The emperor was just then reading memorials from censorate officials commending Toghto's achievements in controlling the river. Jia Lu's merits were discussed next. He was specially promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Academician-Expositor of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, rewarded with gold and silks, and ordered that Academician-Recipient Ouyang Xuan of the Hanlin Academy compose a stele commemorating the pacification of the river—honoring Toghto's labors while fully recording Jia Lu's achievements. The text was ordered proclaimed and deposited in the History Office, and honors were extended to three generations of Jia Lu's forebears.
proposals.after: The emperor was just then reading memorials from censorate officials commending Toghto's achievements in controlling the river. Jia Lu's merits were discussed next. He was specially promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and Grand Academician of the Hall of Worthies, rewarded with gold and silks, and ordered that Academician-Recipient Ouyang Xuan of the Hanlin Academy compose a stele commemorating the pacification of the river—honoring Toghto's labors while fully recording Jia Lu's achievements. The text was ordered proclaimed and deposited in the History Office, and honors were extended to three generations of Jia Lu's forebears.
proposals.reason: 集賢大學士 is Grand Academician of Jixian, not Academician-Expositor.

proposals.before: Soon afterward he was appointed left vice grand councillor and accompanied Toghto in pacifying Xuzhou. After Toghto withdrew his army, Jia Lu was ordered to pursue remnant rebels and divide his forces to attack Haozhou. Pacification Commissioner Yexekä'r joined him as overall military commander. Jia Lu addressed the troops: "By imperial order I command the eight Han guard units. We have camped before Haozhou for seven days already.
proposals.after: Soon afterward he was appointed left vice grand councillor and accompanied Toghto in pacifying Xuzhou. After Toghto withdrew his army, Jia Lu was ordered to pursue remnant rebels and divide his forces to attack Haozhou. Pingzhang Yexekä'r, serving as overall military commander, joined him in supervising the campaign. Jia Lu addressed the troops: "By imperial order I command the eight Han guard units. We have camped before Haozhou for seven days already.
proposals.reason: Chinese 平章 is the office pingzhang (manager of government affairs), not Pacification Commissioner (宣慰使).

proposals.before: He replied: "Empress Zhenge in Emperor Wuzong's reign already received the jade register, and thus was Empress of Wuzong; the two empresses of Mingzong and Wenzong were by nature concubines.
proposals.after: He replied: "Empress Zhenge in Emperor Wuzong's reign already received the jade register, and thus was Empress of Wuzong; the two mothers of Mingzong and Wenzong were by nature concubines.
proposals.reason: 二母后 means the two mothers (of Mingzong and Wenzong), not empresses belonging to Mingzong and Wenzong.

proposals.before: Academician-Expositor Chen Hao of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, who had long resented Luceng, objected: "Emperor Taizong of Tang ennobled the mother of Prince Cao as empress—were there not then two empresses? Why should this not be permitted?"
proposals.after: Grand Academician Chen Hao of the Hall for Advancing Worthies, who had long resented Luceng, objected: "Emperor Taizong of Tang enregistered the mother of Prince Cao Ming as empress—were there not then two empresses? Why should this not be permitted?"
proposals.reason: 集賢大學士 is Grand Academician, not Academician-Expositor; 曹王明 is Prince Cao Ming, omitting the given name 明.

proposals.before: Reappointed investigating censor, he impeached Grand Guardian Dashihaiya, Grand Guardian Ajila, Right Vice Councillor Gongbuban, Minister of Punishments Utuman, Investigating Censor Jidangpu, Court Commissioners Harqanju and Yelü Buhua, and Director Lü Sicheng. All were dismissed.
proposals.after: Reappointed investigating censor, he impeached Grand Guardian Dashihaiya, Grand Guardian Ajila, Right Vice Councillor Gongbuban, Minister of Punishments Utuman, Investigating Censor Jidangpu, Court Commissioners Harqanju and Yuelubuhua, and Director Lü Sicheng. All were dismissed.
proposals.reason: 月魯不花 is the Mongol name Yuelubuhua (Yol-buqa), not the Khitan surname Yelü (耶律).

proposals.before: In 1352 Chancellor Toghto campaigned against the Xuzhou rebels. Because government troops were unaccustomed to the local climate, he recruited coastal salt workers as soldiers. Luceng was specially promoted to Grand Master for the Good of the Heir Apparent and pacification commissioner of Huainan, placed in charge of the punitive campaign, and five thousand salt workers he recruited were sent with the army.
proposals.after: In 1352 Chancellor Toghto campaigned against the Xuzhou rebels. Because government troops were unaccustomed to the local climate, he recruited coastal salt workers as soldiers. Luceng was specially promoted to Grand Master of Assisting Virtue and pacification commissioner of Huainan, placed in charge of the punitive campaign, and five thousand salt workers he recruited were sent with the army.
proposals.reason: 資善大夫 is a prestige title (Grand Master of Assisting Virtue), not an office of the Heir Apparent.

proposals.before: Shitai made secret inquiries and learned that a villager named Shen Ding, returning from carrying goods to Hangzhou, had cast nets in the sea and was killed by fishermen when he stole fish from their nets. Shi had never killed anyone or seized goods, and Gao knew nothing of the affair. The innocence of both men was established.
proposals.after: Shitai made secret inquiries and learned that a villager named Shen Ding, returning from carrying goods to Hangzhou, stole fish from nets fishermen had cast in the sea and was killed by those fishermen. Shi had never killed anyone or seized goods, and Gao knew nothing of the affair. The innocence of both men was established.
proposals.reason: Chinese 漁者張網海中 makes the fishermen the net-casters; both English versions wrongly make Shen Ding cast the nets.

proposals.before: Shitai secretly inquired and learned that Shen Ding of the village, carrying goods to Hangzhou and returning, had cast nets in the sea; because he stole fish from the nets he was killed by the fishermen; Shi in truth had never killed men or seized goods, and Gao also did not know— their wrongful guilt was all cleared.
proposals.after: Shitai secretly inquired and learned that Shen Ding of the village, carrying goods to Hangzhou and returning, stole fish from nets that fishermen had spread in the sea and was killed by the fishermen; Shi in truth had never killed men or seized goods, and Gao also did not know—their wrongful guilt was all cleared.
proposals.reason: Literal English assigns 張網 to Shen Ding; the Chinese subject of 張網 is 漁者.

proposals.before: His father Yingji, during the Zhida period when Renzong was crown prince, was summoned to audience and presented an Ode to the Primal Origin of the Sovereign. He spoke of it to Wuzong and was appointed Hanlin attendant.
proposals.after: His father Yingji, during the Zhida period when Renzong was crown prince, was summoned to audience and presented an Ode to the Primal Origin of the Sovereign. Renzong spoke of him to Wuzong, and he was appointed Hanlin attendant.
proposals.reason: 為言于武宗 is the crown prince (Renzong) recommending Yingji to Wuzong, not Yingji speaking about the ode.

proposals.before: His father Yingji, during the Zhida period when Renzong was crown prince, was summoned for audience, presented an Ode to the Primal Origin of the Sovereign, spoke of it to Wuzong, and was made Hanlin attendant.
proposals.after: His father Yingji, during the Zhida period when Renzong was crown prince, was summoned for audience and presented an Ode to the Primal Origin of the Sovereign; Renzong spoke of him to Wuzong, and he was made Hanlin attendant.
proposals.reason: The silent subject of 為言于武宗 is Renzong recommending Yingji, not Yingji as speaker to Wuzong.

proposals.before: When censors memorialized that censorial oversight should employ close ministers of the court, he was specially appointed commissioner of the Guangdong Surveillance Commission.
proposals.after: When censors memorialized that censorial oversight should employ close ministers of the court, he was specially appointed assistant commissioner of the Guangdong Surveillance Commission.
proposals.reason: 僉廣東廉訪司事 is a signatory/assistant post, not the full surveillance commissioner.

proposals.before: Censor-in-Chief Yesun Temür was then campaigning in the south with a great army but violated discipline and lost troops. Liu Xizeng and nine other investigating censors of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat jointly impeached him.
proposals.after: Censor-in-Chief Yesun Temür was then campaigning in the south with a great army but violated discipline and lost troops. Liu Xizeng and nine other investigating censors of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate jointly impeached him.
proposals.reason: 陝西行臺 is the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, not a Branch Secretariat.

proposals.before: At that time Censor-in-Chief Yesun Temür led a great army south in campaign but violated discipline and lost troops; Liu Xizeng and nine other investigating censors of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat jointly impeached him.
proposals.after: At that time Censor-in-Chief Yesun Temür led a great army south in campaign but violated discipline and lost troops; Liu Xizeng and nine other investigating censors of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate jointly impeached him.
proposals.reason: 陝西行臺 is the branch censorate (xingtai), not a secretariat.

proposals.before: When the Changqiang Suonan rebels seized Ningguo, Boqi and his staff went out in panic to meet them, then fled. Reaching Hangzhou he was appointed minister of war but did not take up the post and was instead appointed surveillance commissioner of western Zhe.
proposals.after: When the Changqiang leader Suonanban seized Ningguo, Boqi and his staff went out in panic to meet them, then fled. Reaching Hangzhou he was appointed minister of war but did not take up the post and was instead appointed surveillance commissioner of western Zhe.
proposals.reason: 長槍鎖南班 names the Long-Spear commander 鎖南班 rather than a generic band label Changqiang Suonan.

proposals.before: An edict stripped them of military command. Dang was appointed general administrator of Fuzhou circuit and Zhao of Linjiang circuit, and both were ordered to supply Pacification Commissioner Huonijichi's army.
proposals.after: An edict stripped them of military command. Dang was appointed general administrator of Fuzhou circuit and Zhao of Linjiang circuit, and both were ordered to supply Pingzhang Huonijichi's army.
proposals.reason: Chinese 平章 is the Yuan office pingzhang (manager of government), not Pacification Commissioner.

decisions.reason: 轉 is a lateral transfer, 判官 is the assistant-prefect (panguan) post, and 陝西行臺 is the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, not a branch secretariat.
